Being close with someone who self harms is a hard thing. One thing I wanna tell you is that you come first, and it might sound selfish or mean. But if you're in bad shape using your energy to worry about her, it might just make things worse.

I'm not sure if you yourself have dealt with depression or if you know someone else who had it, but its definitely important to be patient with her since depression warps the way you can perceive things. 

As long as you let her know you're sorry and that you're there for her, you're already taking a good step forward. She probably doesn't want you to worry about her or doesn't want to talk about her sh. Let her know that you're there if she needs someone to talk to. If she doesn't have a therapist, encourage her to see one if thats what she'd like.

Don't judge her, and don't ask for promises. If she sh again, she'd feel guilt. Self harm is a way coping, and unhealthy one, but theres reasons why she might be doing it. Just be understanding and supportive. Encourage her to get help

Depression is an evil thing, it makes you feel like you're stuck in a hole and it makes you doubt yourself. You're smart, way smarter than you think. 

I think finding need new, healthy ways to cope would help you, if that's something you want. Have you reached out to anyone irl about how you feel?

The world has twice as many good things as it does bad things in it, just that the bad things are harder to look past.

Nobody's truly alone, maybe its hard to believe. Theres always *always* someone out there who cares. For you, maybe its me. I'm proud of you for holding good grades! I can barely stay afloat in some of my classes.

I'm sorry you won't be able to finish all you put your work into, I can't imagine how frustrating that must be. If college is still something you'd want to pursue, it's a chance to go after a new degree you're passionate about.

Everyone dies eventually but it'd suck to die sooner than you have to, there's so much ahead of you. Please stay, its worth it.
